profile.headline: Scientific Instrumentation Software Engineer
profile.summary: I tackle interdisciplinary problems at the intersection of biology, materials science, and engineering using my expertise in surface science, nanotechnology, and microfabrication. I am particularly interested in the development and manufacture of electrochemical biosensors and integrated microfluidic systems.

positions.title: Graduate Student Researcher - Chemical Engineering
positions.description:
PhD in Chemical Engineering.
My thesis research focused on biomimetic supported lipid bilayers in high-density, planar arrays on porous silica, as well as on suspensions of micro- and nanoparticles.   These hybrid organic-inorganic surfaces recapitulate vital characteristics of living cell membranes and present an important tool for the study of cell membrane biophysics, drug-screening, and bio-sensing.

volunteerExperiences.role: Member of the Board of Directors for Greater Bay Area Chapter, Advocacy Team
volunteerExperiences.description: Our goal is to meet with Members of Congress, Health Aides, and Legislative staff to secure funding for diabetes research. Our work has helped direct more than $2 Billion in federal funding toward T1D research since 1998 through the Special Diabetes Program (SDP), which currently provides the National Institutes of Health with $150 million/year for such research.

volunteerExperiences.role: Volunteering as member of Speakers Bureau, Research Information Volunteer (RIV), Advocacy Committee
